issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: the template Main and the UML/problem statement imply single-argument constructors for animals (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")), while the solution classes (Animal, Seal, Pig, Goat) define constructors requiring (String name, int age). This difference will confuse students about the expected constructor signature and will prevent using the example instantiations from the template Main as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor expectations consistent: either change the solution constructors to single-argument (String name) to match the UML/template Main examples, or update the problem statement and template Main to show and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and document the additional 'age' attribute. Preferably remove the extra age parameter from the solution to align with the UML and template examples.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch: the problem statement and UML define Animal with a single attribute 'name', but the solution's Animal class introduces an additional 'age' attribute. This extra attribute changes required constructors and getters/setters and is not documented in the problem description or template, causing potential confusion about the class design.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal class attributes with the problem UML: either remove the 'age' field from the solution and keep only 'name', or update the problem statement and UML to include and describe the 'age' attribute (and update template example instantiations accordingly). Ensure constructors and documentation reflect the chosen attribute set.
